stated: Make the benefits system work better for disabled people by: Giving disabled people and organisations representing them a stronger voice in the design of benefits policies and processes. Bringing Work Capability Assessments in-house. Reforming Personal Independence Payment assessments to make the process more transparent and stop unnecessary reassessments, and end the use of informal assessments.

source.quote: Make the benefits system work better for disabled people by: Giving disabled people and organisations representing them a stronger voice in the design of benefits policies and processes. Bringing Work Capability Assessments in-house. Reforming Personal Independence Payment assessments to make the process more transparent and stop unnecessary reassessments, and end the use of informal assessments.

bearing_set.reason: PIP is a direct cash supplement for the extra costs of disability; fairer assessments and fewer unnecessary reassessments means more disabled people retain or access income that bears materially on their ability to afford essentials.

Work Capability Assessments determine whether disabled claimants face work-related conditionality or receive employment support; bringing them in-house and reforming the process directly affects the employment status and income security of disabled workers and claimants.

The policy directly addresses due process and equal treatment for disabled people: making assessments more transparent, stopping arbitrary reassessments, and giving disabled people and representative organisations a formal voice in policy design all bear on fair/equal treatment and due process for a protected group.

Ending 'informal assessments' — a practice where assessors covertly observe claimants without their knowledge — removes a specific form of covert state surveillance of individuals; this is a concrete, mechanistic improvement to privacy and freedom from unannounced state monitoring.

membership_note: The core effects are on equal treatment/due process (O9) and on removal of covert surveillance of claimants (O10). The policy reforms assessment process and governance, not eligibility criteria or benefit rates, so any income effect on O2 is too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar at this stage. Fiscal/O12 effects are indeterminate (in-housing WCAs has competing cost and saving arguments) and not sufficiently pinned to include.
